content:
Facts: Deceased's siblings and mother challenged holographic will appointing lifelong friend sole heir claiming deceased incapable understanding/willing due to chronic alcohol abuse; alternatively, mother (pretermitted heir) sought reduction for legitimate portion infringement; plaintiffs alleged will drafted ioci causa while intoxicated as deceased habitually wrote joke wills on bar napkins.
Legal Framework: Articles 537, 542, 556-558, 591(2)(3) Italian Civil Code (legitimate portions; estate formation; reduction; testamentary incapacity); Art. 95 Criminal Code (chronic intoxication definition); case law on incapacity standard (Cass. 12691/2017, 27351/2014, 1444/2003).
Interpretive Issues: Evidentiary standard proving natural testamentary incapacity; distinction between habitual drunkenness and chronic alcohol intoxication; whether episodic alcohol abuse sufficient establishing total incapacity; probative weight of will content regarding testator's capacity assessment; burden allocation proving incapacity versus capacity presumption; whether pretermitted heir acquires heir status before or after successful reduction; effect of pre-publication inheritance renunciation by pretermitted heir; reinstatement modality (in-kind co-ownership versus monetary quantification) for legitimate portion.
Principles Applied: Natural incapacity requires complete deprivation of action-awareness or self-determination capacity due to temporary/permanent infirmity or disruptive cause, not mere mental/intellectual faculty anomaly/alteration. Incapacity severity must justify interdiction if habitual. Capacity constitutes rule, incapacity exception; challenger bears rigorous precise proof burden unless total permanent incapacity proven (then proponent proves lucid-interval drafting). Habitual drunkenness insufficient excluding capacity as normally temporary condition involving temporary mental-faculty reduction. Chronic drug intoxication affects entire behavior permanently characterizing illness excluding/diminishing capacity regardless of continued substance intake. Medical documentation showing episodic (not chronic) alcohol intoxication; hospital admission rehabilitation noting absent typical withdrawal symptoms incompatible with chronic intoxication. Valid driving license suspension/return following medical commission assessment incompatible with total incapacity allegation. Employment as bartender one month post-will drafts contra incapacity claim. Joke-will allegations insufficiently proven; sole witness testimony regarding improvised napkin notes contradicted by other witnesses denying knowledge. Witness's intoxicated state during alleged will-drafting occasion undermines recollection reliability. Will content assessment mandatory; judge considers seriousness, normality, consistency of provisions plus inspiring feelings/purposes. Testamentary intent favoring childhood friend over estranged relatives (due to unresolved boarding-school trauma, rehabilitation pressure) consistent with relationships, not extravagant. Pretermitted heir lacks heir status before successful reduction action finality; acquisition conditional/deferred pending constitutive reduction judgment. Pre-publication renunciation tamquam non esset absent hereditary bequest at time; filing reduction action insufficient immediately determining heir-status acquisition. Renunciation impossible when inheritance non-devolved due to pretermission. Reduction grants in-kind reinstatement creating co-ownership share in relictum assets absent division request. Judge declares estate assets and abstract co-ownership shares due each legitimate heir becoming necessary heir. Monetary quantification serves only infringement-assessment tool, not reinstatement mechanism. Reduction judgment requires transcription ordering in public registers (property/companies) for undivided inherited-property co-ownership shares.
